exchanges.q: Before I turn anything over — is there something particular you would like to look at?
exchanges.a: the flat, I suppose. there is a decision coming up on it

gate.reading_of_them: The flat, and a decision coming up on it.

exchanges.q: The situation card is the Eight of Cups. What does it look like it is pointing at for you?
exchanges.a: someone walking away from a set of cups they stacked themselves

gate.reading_of_them: They see someone walking away from cups they stacked themselves.

exchanges.q: What is it about the way they are stacked that reads as their own to you?
exchanges.a: they are neat. nobody stacks someone else's things that neatly

gate.reading_of_them: The neatness is what makes the stack theirs.

exchanges.q: Whose neat stack is that, in your world — yours, or one you are living in?
exchanges.a: the flat, mostly. I have had it four years and I know where everything is

gate.reading_of_them: The flat, four years, and knowing where everything is.

exchanges.q: Living around a desk that has not moved in four years — how have things been?
exchanges.a: the desk, under the window. easy, mostly. that is sort of the point

gate.reading_of_them: The desk has not moved, and that is the point.

exchanges.q: Four years is a while to know where everything is. The obstacle card lands now — the Two of Swords. What do you see in it?
exchanges.a: someone deciding with their eyes shut

gate.reading_of_them: Someone deciding with their eyes shut.

exchanges.q: What is it about them that reads as eyes-shut to you?
exchanges.a: the blindfold, and the swords are crossed so neither one wins

gate.reading_of_them: The blindfold, and the crossed swords where neither wins.

exchanges.q: Whose deciding-with-the-eyes-shut is that one?
exchanges.a: the lease is up in March and renewing costs more than I make, so I would be moving across town from Dana

gate.reading_of_them: The lease is up in March, renewing is unaffordable, and moving means leaving Dana behind.

exchanges.q: What happened the last time a lease came up?
exchanges.a: nothing. I open the listings and close them again

gate.reading_of_them: They open the listings and close them again.

exchanges.q: Opening them and closing them again is its own kind of answer. The advice card is the Six of Swords. What do you see in it?
exchanges.a: a crossing, and someone else is doing the rowing

gate.reading_of_them: A crossing where someone else does the rowing.

exchanges.q: What is it about the rowing that reads as someone else's to you?
exchanges.a: he is facing the other way and she is not holding an oar

gate.reading_of_them: He faces away and she holds no oar.

exchanges.q: Whose rowing is that one?
exchanges.a: I keep waiting for someone to tell me it is fine either way

gate.reading_of_them: They are waiting to be told it is fine either way.

exchanges.q: What would it take for you to say it is fine either way yourself?
exchanges.a: I would have to work out what I am actually protecting

gate.reading_of_them: They would have to work out what they are protecting.

exchanges.q: Across these three cards, in your own words: a neat stack you built, a decision made with the eyes shut, and a crossing where someone else is doing the rowing. This week, notice the moment you reach for someone to tell you it is fine either way.
exchanges.a: yeah. I have been building a little scheduling thing on the side, to stop myself opening the listings

gate.reading_of_them: They have been building a scheduling tool on the side.

exchanges.q: So you built a scheduler. What does the scheduler put in the evenings?
exchanges.a: blocks, mostly. something booked so the evening is spoken for

gate.reading_of_them: The scheduler books blocks into the evenings.

exchanges.q: What did you write the scheduler in?
exchanges.a: python, and a text file

gate.reading_of_them: Python and a text file.

exchanges.q: Python and a text file. What made you pick a text file over a database?
exchanges.a: a database felt like overkill for one person

gate.reading_of_them: A database felt like overkill.

exchanges.q: Which part of the scheduler would you port to the phone?
exchanges.a: the reminders, probably. I want the reminders on the phone

gate.reading_of_them: They want the reminders on the phone.

exchanges.q: The table has turned one more card — the Ace of Pentacles, the last one. What do you see in it?
exchanges.a: a hand holding a coin out of a cloud

gate.reading_of_them: A hand holding a coin out of a cloud.

exchanges.q: What is it about the hand that reads as holding out to you?
exchanges.a: it is not putting it down anywhere. someone has to take it

gate.reading_of_them: Nobody has taken what the hand is holding out.

session.closing_reflection: Across these four cards, in your own words: a neat stack, a decision with the eyes shut, a crossing someone else is rowing, and now a hand holding something out that nobody has taken. This week, notice the moment you wait to be handed it.
